definitions.explanation: A discolored mark on the skin caused by an injury where blood vessels are damaged beneath the surface.
A colored mark on the skin that is present from birth or appears shortly after.

examples.english: I got a bruise on my arm.

examples.japanese: ぶつけたところに{大|おお}きなあざが{残|のこ}っている。
examples.english: A large bruise remains where I bumped it.

examples.japanese: あざが{消|き}えるまで{一週間|いっしゅうかん}くらいかかった。
examples.english: It took about a week for the bruise to disappear.

examples.japanese: {生|う}まれつきのあざがある。
{背中|せなか}にあざがある{赤|あか}ちゃんは{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Many babies have birthmarks on their backs.

examples.japanese: {蒙古斑|もうこはん}は{青|あお}いあざのように{見|み}えるが、{成長|せいちょう}とともに{消|き}える。
examples.english: Mongolian spots look like blue birthmarks but fade as the child grows.

notes: Can be written in kanji as {痣|あざ}, but the kana form is more common. The typical verb pattern is あざができる (a bruise forms) rather than あざがつく. For bruises, {青|あお}あざ (blue bruise) is a common compound. In medical contexts, birthmarks may be further classified by color: {青|あお}あざ, {赤|あか}あざ, {茶|ちゃ}あざ, etc.
